newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Modigliani sees Buba keeping Germany out of EMU.
newsitem.headline: Modigliani sees Buba keeping Germany out of EMU.

text.p: Nobel prize-winning economist Franco Modigliani said he believed the Bundesbank would succeed in keeping Germany out of Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU).

"The news that Germany risks not to meet EMU criteria has shaken Europe," Modigliani, economist at the Massachussetts Institute of Technology (MIT), said in a column in the Swedish newspaper Svenska Dagbladet on Wednesday.

"For us that is no surprise. On the contrary, it confirms our two year old theory that the Bundesbank in the end will win the struggle with the Chancellor about keeping Germany outside the monetary union."
The Bundesbank has no interest in letting the euro replace the mark, he said, adding that the Bundesbank has functioned as the central bank for Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM).
The Bundesbank has denied repeatedly that it is opposed to EMU.
The bank does insist that the economic terms set for the creation of a stable currency must be met for the project to go ahead.

"With a single European currency, the situation would be very different because monetary and currency policy would be decided by the European central bank, in which Germany would be a heavyweight, but not have the absolute monetary power," Modigliani said.
This position is in conflict with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's aim to realise the Maastricht treaty, he said.

"...we have put forward as a theory what people are now starting to recognise as a possibility -- that Germany at the last minute will find a 'technical' reason for not joining the monetary union, for example by pointing out that the budget deficit is 3.1 percent instead of 3.0 percent," Modigliani said.
But the EMU could theoretically start without Germany if only France would devalue the franc and Britain would give up its isolationism, Modigliani said.
However he said these two moves did not seem likely.
